context: Figure 3a shows the X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of Cu2 S and RGO-Cu2 S samples. Subsequently, the diffraction peaks of the as-synthesized samples can be indexed to Cu2 S (JCPDS No. 33-0490) with observed diffraction peaks at 2θ = 27.2°, 29.2°, 30.9°, 32.3° and 47.9°, corresponding well with those of lattice planes (104), (132), (041), (141) and (532) of monoclinic phase (Figure 3a ).[ 45 ] It was noted that the intensities of Cu 2S diffraction peaks were decreased with the increase of RGO amount, mainly due to the covering of RGO nanosheets onto the surface of Cu2 S microspheres (Figure 1d ). On the basis of the thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), the RGO mass ratios of the three RGO-Cu2 S composites were 26.8, 41.4, and 55.3%, respectively. Compared to Cu2 S , the RGO-Cu2 S -2 exhibited obvious carbon signal except copper and sulfur elements (Figure S4, Supporting Information), verifi ed by the measurement of energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDS).
